candidate.answerReason: A point 10 feet above the bottom forms an equilateral triangle with the center and bottom point. The first arrival requires a 60-degree rotation, taking one sixth of 60 seconds.

methods.label: Recognize an equilateral triangle
methods.explanation:
At a constant rotation rate, time is proportional to the angle turned. We first find the angle needed to reach the specified height.

Let \(O\) be the center, \(B\) the bottom point, and \(P\) a point on the wheel \(10\) feet above \(B\). Let the horizontal line through \(P\) meet \(OB\) at \(H\). Since \(OB=20\), we have \(BH=OH=10\). Thus \(PH\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(OB\).

A point on a perpendicular bisector is equally distant from the segment’s endpoints, so \(PO=PB\). Also, \(PO=OB=20\), since both are radii. Hence all three sides of \(\triangle OPB\) are equal, giving
\[
\angle BOP=60^\circ.
\]
The two points at this height lie on opposite sides of the vertical diameter. In either direction, the rider first reaches one after turning \(60^\circ\), or one sixth of a revolution. A full revolution takes \(60\) seconds, so the time is
\[
\frac16\cdot60=\boxed{10\text{ seconds}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Perpendicular-bisector and equilateral-triangle properties determine the angle using elementary geometry; proportional time then gives the answer.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task connects the rider’s rotated radius with an elapsed fraction of a revolution. Equal radii and minute-second conversion support that connection. Perpendicular-bisector reasoning and equilateral-triangle recognition are the specific geometric procedures used by this method.

review.mathematicalCheck: The horizontal line through P bisects OB perpendicularly, so PO=PB. Together with PO=OB=20, this makes OPB equilateral. The first arrival in either direction requires 60 degrees, taking 60/6=10 seconds.
